historical_accepted_route.actual_current_prototype_strategy: Separate below and above counts. Removing the removable i-node A changes the total addable-minus-removable count by the Cartan column, and A becomes an addable node in mu^A. Splitting all remaining i-nodes into strictly above and strictly below A gives d_A(mu)+d^A(mu^A)=d_i(mu)+1. Induction from the empty diagram and the same local boundary changes gives d_i(mu)=(Lambda0-alpha,alpha_i). Expanding defect(alpha)-defect(alpha-alpha_i) using (alpha_i,alpha_i)=2 gives d_i(mu)+1. Induct on the number of nodes in the degree/codegree recursion to obtain their sum equal to defect. For a horizontal terminal brick, codegree counts strictly ABOVE it: the first row has no such nodes; an e-brick contains every residue once and above boundary addable/removable contributions cancel. This proves both brick clauses. Check e2 shape(2): below degree1, above codegree0, defect1; shape(1,1): degree0, above codegree1, defect1. These checks illustrate, not replace, the boundary count proof. No choice.

edits.before:
1.1 **Counting addable and removable nodes (1).** Delete the removable $i$-node $A$ from $\mu$; in $\mu^A$ the node $A$ itself is addable, and no node strictly below $A$ changes its addable or removable status, because the shape on and below the row of $A$ is unchanged there [F1]. Among the $i$-nodes strictly above $A$, only the two nodes adjacent to $A$ in the row above can change status, and they change simultaneously: the node directly above $A$'s column becomes removable in $\mu^A$ exactly when the node one step to its right becomes addable, both conditions being $\mu_{r-1}=\mu_r$ for $A$ in row $r$ [F1]. Hence the number of addable $i$-nodes strictly above $A$ minus removable ones is the same in $\mu^A$ as in $\mu$, and $d_A(\mu)+d^A(\mu^A)=\#\{\text{addable }i\text{-nodes of }\mu\}-\#\{\text{removable }i\text{-nodes of }\mu\}+1=d_i(\mu)+1$, the $+1$ recording that $A$ was removable in $\mu$ and is addable in $\mu^A$. [F1, F2]

1.2 **The Cartan formula (2).** For the empty partition $d_i=0=(\Lambda_0,\alpha_i)$ because $\alpha=0$; adding one node of residue $i$ changes the left side by $d_i(\mu)-d_i(\mu^A)=1$ and the right side by $-(\alpha_i,\alpha_i)=-2$ relative to $\Lambda_0-(\alpha-\alpha_i)$, i.e. by $(\Lambda_0-\alpha,\alpha_i)-(\Lambda_0-\alpha+\alpha_i,\alpha_i)=-2$; the two differences agree, so induction on $d$ proves the identity for every partition [F1, F3]. [F1, F3]
edits.after:
1.1 **Counting addable and removable nodes (1).** Deleting the removable node $A$ of residue $i$ makes $A$ addable. Apart from this change, all corner changes occur immediately next to $A$ and have residues $i-1$ or $i+1$, which differ from $i$ since $e\ge2$ (for $e=2$ the two neighbor residues coincide with each other). Hence the signed count of $i$-nodes strictly above $A$ is unchanged, as is the signed count strictly below it. There is no other addable or removable $i$-node in the row of $A$. Splitting the signed corner count of $\mu$ into its above and below parts and the removable node $A$ therefore gives $d_A(\mu)+d^A(\mu^A)=d_i(\mu)+1$. [F1, F2]

1.2 **The Cartan formula (2).** Write $u_j$ for the basis vector indexed by $j\in\mathbb Z/e\mathbb Z$ in the free abelian group on residues, and choose $R$ greater than the number of nonzero rows of $\mu$. Put $b_r=\mu_r-r$. The signed corner vector is $\sum_i d_i(\mu)u_i=u_{-R}+\sum_{r=1}^R(u_{b_r+1}-u_{b_r})$: adjacent row-boundary terms cancel precisely when the corresponding node is not a corner, and the tail term cancels the artificial bottom boundary. For the empty partition this telescopes to $u_0$, so $d_i(\varnothing)=\delta_{i,0}=(\Lambda_0,\alpha_i)$. Adding a node of residue $j$ moves one $b_r=j-1$ to $j$ and changes this vector by $u_{j+1}-2u_j+u_{j-1}$. Thus each $d_i$ changes by $-a_{ij}$, including the double neighbor contribution when $e=2$. The vector with coordinates $(\Lambda_0-\alpha,\alpha_i)$ has the same initial value and the same change when $\alpha$ increases by $\alpha_j$. Induction on the number of nodes proves (2). [F1, F3]
